name: OpenWrt
author: Netlens
description: Reads an OpenWrt router or access point: the router itself as a network node, and every device it knows as a client: DHCP leases and neighbours (wired), and the Wi-Fi stations that are associated with each radio, with band, signal strength (RSSI) and link speed. Netlens uses this to place devices in the hierarchy and to show Wi-Fi signal history and roaming. Read-only: it only calls a few read functions through the router's ubus web interface.

info.title: Set up the router (once)
info.text: Netlens talks to OpenWrt's ubus over HTTP(S), the same way LuCI does. Install the packages below, then either use root or create a login that may only read what Netlens needs (recommended). Wi-Fi details need the iwinfo module.
info.code:
# 1. as root on the router: the luci-rpc calls and the web server for ubus
apk add uhttpd-mod-ubus rpcd-mod-iwinfo luci-base     # opkg install ... on OpenWrt before 25.12

# 2. a login that can only read what Netlens needs
cat > /usr/share/rpcd/acl.d/netlens.json <<'EOF2'
{"netlens": {"description": "Netlens, read only",
  "read": {"ubus": {"luci-rpc": ["getHostHints", "getDHCPLeases", "getWirelessDevices"],
                    "system": ["board"], "network.interface": ["dump"], "network.device": ["status"],
                    "iwinfo": ["info", "assoclist"]}}}}
EOF2
echo 'netlens:x:1500:1500:netlens:/var:/bin/false' >> /etc/passwd
echo 'netlens:x:0:0:99999:7:::' >> /etc/shadow
passwd netlens                                          # choose a password
uci add rpcd login; uci set rpcd.@login[-1].username=netlens
uci set rpcd.@login[-1].password='$p$netlens'; uci add_list rpcd.@login[-1].read=netlens
uci commit rpcd; /etc/init.d/rpcd restart

config.label: Routers and access points
config.help: One line per OpenWrt device. List the main router and every OpenWrt access point; give each access point the address of the router it is plugged into under 'Uplink' so the hierarchy is right.

columns.label: Role
columns.help: auto: a device with an active WAN interface is the gateway, any other is an access point.

columns.label: Uplink (address of its parent)
columns.help: For an access point: the address of the OpenWrt router (or the node) it is connected to.

config.label: Verify TLS certificate
config.help: Only for https addresses. OpenWrt makes a self-signed certificate.
